workLog.entry: Implemented Option 1 (Claude-side per-group in-process dispatcher) and reported it green. Overclaim: 'parity' was based on the dispatcher's own gate/observe tests, not fidelity to Claude host semantics.
Independent review flagged 6 blocking defects. Did not defend; re-opened the architecture and prioritized deletion/configuration over addition.

Confirmed defects: (1) concatenated JSON stdout is invalid and dropped (GitHub docs + topical_memory_injection/correction_applier emit JSON); (2) Stop and UserPromptSubmit are blocking per hook_contracts.py but were forced observe; (3) _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SEC=5 fabricates aggregate ceilings vs Claude ~60s; (4) regeneration nesting footgun; (5) no build_all/drift ownership, copy_bootstrap only-if-missing drift; (6) group_key collision + trust of stale manifests.

Research subagent + GitHub Copilot CLI docs: hooks from all sources run additively; NO per-source disable flag; disableAllHooks is nuclear; removing the settings.json hooks key is the only 'plugin-only' path. The batched plugin dispatcher (ADR-068) is valid because it emits one merged decision; the in-process Claude clone is not.

Determination: runtime gap + configuration, not code. Reverted the 10 flawed commits (git reset --hard origin/main; unpushed). Wrote .agents/analysis/2026-07-14-hook-batching-determination.md documenting findings, the runtime gap, the config options (A per-user disableAllHooks; B remove settings.json hooks key + enabledPlugins; C machine config), corrected invalid claims, and preserved the still-valid audit facts.

nextSteps: Owner decision: apply config A (per-user, immediate unblock) now; decide on config B (structural, distribution-wide) which is an enforcement-policy change for in-repo Claude Code.
Do not reintroduce Claude-side in-process hook batching.
If Copilot-side scoping of advisory hooks is still desired, do it in the plugin dispatcher (which already emits one valid merged decision), not by cloning batching onto the Claude repo-settings path.
